segments.note: The why text retains forced acceptance invention, linter-only acceptances, and plan-graph pollution.
The Claim heading becomes the identify/derive step in prefer; no independent instruction is lost.
The Bind heading becomes the exact-identity instruction in prefer.
The usable header form is generalized in prefer; the original example remains in audit.
The usable train header form is generalized in prefer; the original example remains in audit.
The Avoid heading is represented by the avoid collection.
The rebinding-for-attribution prohibition remains explicit; the declared clarification distinguishes truthful correction consistently with deriving the binding from what the test proves.
The Verify heading is represented by concrete verification criteria in evidence.

activation.note: Scope remains stack-neutral URN-carrying test files, with no-URN files and plan-graph existence checks excluded. Presence, journey/E2E binding-kind eligibility, and truthfulness are distinguished; header scanning is observable, classification needs an observer, and semantic truthfulness is judgment-based. The Train exception does not bypass truthfulness.

audit.summary: All 44 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with structural headings and example syntax appropriately compressed. The rewrite retains the truthful-binding obligation, anti-patterns, rationales, and detector boundaries; the shared strict-disposition node is genuinely generic and contains the claimed policy.

segmentChecks.note: Given, then, and activation retain the URN precondition, both accepted binding forms, and the journey/E2E restriction on Train.
Why and verifier_detail require both exercising the declared subject and asserting its required outcome; syntactic validity alone is explicitly insufficient.
The false-coverage hazard and the fact that an unrelated binding can pass the structural detector remain explicit.
Why preserves the causal chain from forced Acceptance bindings to invented linter-only acceptances and plan-graph pollution.
Avoid and activation prohibit selecting or inventing a binding merely for attribution.
The Claim heading is safely absorbed into the derive-and-identify instruction in prefer.
The Bind heading is safely absorbed into prefer's exact-plan-identity header instruction.
Prefer generalizes the Acceptance example without losing its syntax; the concrete source example remains in audit.
Prefer generalizes the Train example without losing its syntax; the concrete source example remains in audit.
The Avoid heading is represented by the avoid collection and all three prohibitions remain.
The prohibition on rebinding for attribution remains, and the clarification correctly distinguishes a truthful stale-binding correction.
The Verify heading is replaced by concrete stimulus and behavioral-witness checks in evidence.
Unless, activation, evidence, and verifier_detail preserve the journey/E2E Train exception without exempting truthfulness.
Verifier_detail and activation keep plan-graph existence outside this per-file detector's scope.
Strict disposition remains in identity, verifier_detail, and audit; the shared node accurately captures the generic fail-on-every-finding policy with no advisory mode or ratchet.

risks: Journey/E2E classification is not operationalized in the coder-facing fields, so a coder who cannot classify the test could choose Train incorrectly; the restriction itself is nevertheless explicit.

unobservable: Whether a test is a journey/E2E test currently requires a new classifier or reviewer judgment.
Whether the test exercises the bound subject and asserts the outcome required by that subject is semantic and LLM/reviewer-judged.
Whether a binding was selected, changed, or invented solely to make the test attributable involves intent or provenance and is not directly observable by Datalog.

review.summary: The rewrite faithfully preserves the structural, binding-kind, and truthfulness obligations, including the anti-patterns, rationale, exceptions, and detector boundaries. Coder-facing guidance is sufficient for the correct implementation, while non-structural activation cases appropriately require classification or semantic judgment rather than pretending to be Datalog-observable.
